name: Standard Chess
desc: Standard FIDE rules

name: Almost Chess
desc: White's Queen is replaced by a Chancellor (Rook + Knight compound).

name: Amazon Chess
desc: Queens replaced by Amazons (Queen + Knight). The most powerful piece possible.

name: Andernach Chess
desc: Capturing pieces change colour. Kings are exempt.

name: Antichess
desc: Captures are mandatory. First to lose all pieces wins.

name: Atomic Chess
desc: Captures cause explosions destroying all pieces on adjacent squares.

name: Benedict Chess
desc: Pieces convert enemies they attack instead of capturing. Win by converting the king.

name: Berolina Chess
desc: Pawns move diagonally and capture straight — the inverse of normal.

name: Berserk Chess
desc: Delivering check grants an immediate bonus move.

name: Breakthrough
desc: Pawns only — first to reach the far side wins. No captures backward.

name: Capablanca Chess
desc: Two extra pieces: Archbishop (B+N) and Chancellor (R+N). Wider board.

name: Checkless Chess
desc: You cannot give check unless it is checkmate.

name: Chigorin
desc: White's Bishops replaced by Knights. Four Knights vs standard army.

name: Codrus
desc: No check exists. You win by getting your own King captured.

name: Courier Chess
desc: Medieval German variant from the 1200s. Extra bishops and sage pieces.

name: Cylinder Chess
desc: Files wrap: a-file connects to h-file. Bishops slide around the cylinder.

name: Dark Chess
desc: Total fog — you can only see your own pieces. Capture the king to win.

name: Diana Chess
desc: 6×6 board with no queens or knights. Bishops and rooks dominate.

name: Dice Chess
desc: A die roll determines which piece type must move each turn.

name: Displacement Chess
desc: Swap positions with adjacent friendly pieces as an alternative move.

name: Duck Chess
desc: After each move, place the duck (blocker) on any empty square.

name: Einstein Chess
desc: Non-capturing moves demote pieces, captures promote them.

name: Endgame Chess
desc: Only Kings and pawns. Pure endgame technique from move one.

name: Extinction Chess
desc: Lose all your knights, bishops, rooks, or pawns — you lose the game.

name: Fischer Random (Chess960)
desc: Back rank pieces randomised (960 positions). Castling rules adapted.

name: Five-Check
desc: Extended Three-Check — five checks wins instead of three.

name: Fog of War Chess
desc: You only see squares your pieces can move to. No check warnings.

name: Giveaway
desc: Forced captures. King is not royal. Stalemate is a loss.

name: Grand Chess
desc: Same new pieces as Capablanca, bigger board, pawns start on rank 3.

name: Grid Chess
desc: Moves must cross at least one grid line (2×2 cells).

name: Half Chess
desc: Compressed 4-rank board. Armies start adjacent — instant contact.

name: Hoppel-Poppel
desc: Knights capture like bishops, bishops capture like knights.

name: Horde Chess
desc: White has a full army. Black has 36 pawns. Asymmetric survival.

name: King of the Hill
desc: Moving your king to d4/d5/e4/e5 is an instant win.

name: Knightmate
desc: Knight and King swap roles. The Knight is royal; Kings move as knights.

name: Legan Chess
desc: Berolina pawns with swapped king/queen starting squares.

name: Los Alamos
desc: First computer chess (1956). 6x6 board, no Bishops, no castling.

name: Madrasi Chess
desc: Same-type opposing pieces that attack each other are paralysed.

name: Maharaja & Sepoys
desc: One player has a full army. The other has one piece that moves as queen + knight.

name: Makpong
desc: King cannot move out of check. You must block or capture instead.

name: Makruk
desc: Thai chess. Promote on rank 6 to Met. No castling or en passant.

name: Marseillais Chess
desc: Each player makes TWO moves per turn (except White's first turn).

name: Minichess
desc: Gardner's 5x5 board. All piece types, fast tactical games.

name: Monster Chess
desc: White moves twice per turn but starts with only King, Rooks, and pawns.

name: No Castling Chess
desc: Standard chess with castling removed. Kings must develop naturally.

name: No Retreat
desc: Pieces cannot move backward toward their own starting rank.

name: Omnicide
desc: Lose all pieces to win. Like Antichess but captures are not forced.

name: Orda Chess
desc: Asymmetric Mongol army with divergent movers vs standard pieces.

name: Patrol Chess
desc: A piece can only capture if defended by a friendly piece.

name: Pawns Only
desc: Kings and pawns only. First to promote wins instantly.

name: Peasants' Revolt
desc: White has King + 8 pawns vs Black's King + 2 Knights + 8 pawns.

name: Petty Chess
desc: All piece types on a compact 5×6 board. Fast tactical games.

name: Progressive
desc: Moves per turn escalate: 1, 2, 3, 4... Check ends your turn early.

name: Racing Kings
desc: No checks allowed. Both kings start on 1st rank. Race to the top.

name: Rifle Chess
desc: Capturing pieces stay on their square — they 'shoot' the target.

name: Shatar
desc: Mongolian chess. No check — win by leaving opponent with a bare king.

name: Single-Check
desc: One check wins. No checkmate needed — any single check ends the game.

name: Stalemate Wins
desc: Standard chess but stalemate is a win, not a draw.

name: Suicide Chess
desc: Forced captures like Giveaway, but stalemate is a draw, not a loss.

name: Three-Check
desc: First to check the opponent three times wins.

name: Toroidal Chess
desc: Board wraps in both directions forming a torus. No edge exists.

name: Torpedo Chess
desc: Pawns can move two squares forward from any rank, not just the starting rank.

name: Upside-Down
desc: Pieces start on the opponent's back rank. Instant tactical chaos.

name: Weak!
desc: The weakest piece type with a legal move must move first.

name: Crazyhouse
desc: Captured pieces switch sides and can be dropped back onto the board.

name: Recruitment Chess
desc: Captured pieces defect to the captor and appear on the vacated square.

name: Teleportation Chess
desc: Each side has 3 teleports — move any piece to any empty square.

name: Poison Chess
desc: Capture squares become toxic for 3 turns — landing on poison destroys pieces.

name: Medusa Chess
desc: Queen petrifies all enemy pieces she attacks for 2 turns — they cannot move.

name: Immunization Chess
desc: Pieces adjacent to a capture become immune to capture for 2 turns.
